newsitem.title: USA: N.Korea apparently cancels missile test, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea apparently cancels missile test, U.S. says.

text.p: North Korea appears to have called off a planned ballistic missile test that the United States had strongly opposed as a threat to regional stability, a senior State Department official said on Thursday.

"We believe that they were making those preparations" to carry out a medium-range missile test "and that they've now stopped the preparations," Charles Kartman, deputy assistant secretary of state for East Asian affairs, said in an interview.

Kartman said North Korea, which had publicly denounced U.S. and other outside complaints about the planned test, appeared to have backed off for now, "but I don't know that those second thoughts are going to be long-lasting ones."

Last month, the State Department said it had sent a "very strong message" to Pyongyang not to carry out the test for fear of stoking instability in Northeast Asia by advancing its extensive ballistic missile development program. On October 23, a statement on the North's Central News Agency said any such test was a matter of North Korean sovereignty "and no one else is entitled or has any ground to meddle with it."

Earlier in the month, Japanese Defense ministry officials said Pyongyang had completed preparations for a test, including sending a frigate into the Sea of Japan to monitor a possible missile splashdown.

Asked whether North Korea had bowed to U.S. pressure, Kartman said: "I would love to believe we have that kind of influence (with the North) and that is a possibility." He added: "My best guess is that they did hear these concerns from us and from others as well, and they had some second thoughts."
